findings.title: Zero-length date overrides are never recognized as closed days
findings.body: The code compares two distinct Dayjs instances with `===`, which is always false even when `date.start` and `date.end` represent the same instant. Date overrides with equal start/end are used to represent an unavailable date, but this branch is skipped; the later bounds checks can leave a slot at that instant available. Compare the timestamps (for example with `isSame`) so an all-day/unavailable override blocks every slot.

findings.title: Fixed-host override validation accepts slots that run past the override end
findings.body: For a matching override date, the new validation rejects slots ending before the override starts and slots starting after the override ends, but never rejects a slot whose start is inside the override and whose end is after `date.end`. A round-robin slot generated from another host can therefore be offered even though the fixed host's override ends before the meeting does, allowing bookings outside that fixed host's availability. The check must require the full `[slotStartTime, slotEndTime]` interval to be contained in the override.

findings.title: Multiple working-hour ranges on a day make fixed hosts unavailable in valid ranges
findings.body: The `find` callback returns true when a slot is outside any working-hour range, and the caller then rejects the slot. With split availability on the same weekday (for example 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00), a 10:00 slot is correctly inside the first range but is before the second range, so the second range causes it to be rejected. This causes round-robin events with fixed hosts and split schedules to hide otherwise valid slots; availability should be accepted when it fits at least one range for that day.

findings.title: Working-hour validation ignores the meeting end time
findings.body: `end` is calculated from `slotStartTime` again rather than from `slotEndTime`. Consequently, the fixed-host check only tests whether the slot starts before the end of a working-hours range and can accept a meeting that extends beyond the fixed host's normal availability. Calculate the end from `slotEndTime` (including the requested duration) before comparing it to `workingHour.endTime`.
